subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In which year was the Warsaw Pact created?
questions.explain: The Warsaw Pact was formed in 1955, partly in response to West Germany joining NATO.

questions.q: Which 1486 treatise became a notorious manual for identifying and prosecuting witches?
questions.explain: The Malleus Maleficarum ('Hammer of Witches'), published in 1486, provided a framework for detecting and trying witches.

questions.q: What does the deterrence concept 'MAD' stand for?
questions.explain: MAD, Mutually Assured Destruction, held that nuclear war would annihilate both sides, deterring attack.

questions.q: In which year did US combat troops complete withdrawal from Vietnam?
questions.explain: Under the 1973 Paris Peace Accords, US combat forces withdrew from Vietnam.

questions.q: Who led the communist victory in China in 1949?
questions.explain: Mao Zedong's Communists won the civil war and proclaimed the People's Republic of China in October 1949.

questions.q: In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
questions.explain: The Berlin Wall was erected in August 1961 to halt the flow of refugees to the West.

questions.q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall and communism collapse across Eastern Europe?
questions.explain: The Berlin Wall fell in November 1989 amid the collapse of communist regimes in Eastern Europe.

questions.q: In which year did Mussolini lead the March on Rome that brought him to power?
questions.explain: The Fascist March on Rome of October 1922 prompted King Victor Emmanuel III to appoint Mussolini Prime Minister.

questions.q: In which year did Napoleon crown himself Emperor of the French?
questions.explain: Napoleon crowned himself Emperor in Notre-Dame on 2 December 1804, in the presence of Pope Pius VII.

questions.q: Roughly when did the Vietnam War's major US involvement intensify?
questions.explain: US combat involvement escalated sharply from the mid-1960s, following the 1964 Gulf of Tonkin incident.

questions.q: Which US president labelled the USSR an 'evil empire' in 1983?
questions.explain: Ronald Reagan called the Soviet Union an 'evil empire' in 1983 during the Second Cold War.

questions.q: Which development is most associated with the decline of witch persecutions after c1680?
options: The spread of the printing press
The growth of scientific rationalism and judicial scepticism
questions.explain: The rise of scientific rationalism and increasing scepticism among judges and elites undermined the legal basis for prosecutions.

questions.q: Which two reform policies are most associated with Gorbachev?
questions.explain: Gorbachev pursued glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring).

questions.q: In which year did the Cuban Missile Crisis occur?
questions.explain: The Cuban Missile Crisis unfolded in October 1962, the closest the superpowers came to nuclear war.

questions.q: In which year did King Louis XVI summon the Estates-General, an act that triggered the chain of events leading to revolution in France?
questions.explain: Facing fiscal collapse, Louis XVI summoned the Estates-General, which first met at Versailles in May 1789 for the first time since 1614.

questions.q: Which three leaders met at the Yalta Conference in February 1945?
questions.explain: The 'Big Three' at Yalta were Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin.

questions.q: What term describes the easing of Cold War tensions in the early 1970s?
questions.explain: Detente denoted the relaxation of US-Soviet tensions, marked by treaties like SALT I in 1972.

questions.q: The Byzantine defeat at which 1071 battle helped prompt the appeal that led to the First Crusade?
questions.explain: The Seljuk Turks crushed the Byzantines at Manzikert in 1071, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement and prompting the appeal to the West.

questions.q: The 1929 agreement that reconciled the Fascist state with the papacy was known as the:
questions.explain: The Lateran Pacts of 1929 recognised Vatican City as an independent state and settled the long-standing 'Roman Question'.

questions.q: What 1968 reform movement did the Warsaw Pact crush in Czechoslovakia?
questions.explain: The Prague Spring's liberal reforms under Dubcek were ended by a Warsaw Pact invasion in August 1968.

questions.q: In which year were the Yalta and Potsdam conferences held?
questions.explain: Both the Yalta (February) and Potsdam (July-August) conferences took place in 1945.

questions.q: Which Italian maritime republic played the dominant role in diverting the Fourth Crusade?
questions.explain: Venice, under Doge Enrico Dandolo, supplied the fleet and redirected the crusade first to Zara and then to Constantinople.

questions.q: In which year did Pope Urban II preach the sermon at Clermont that launched the First Crusade?
questions.explain: Pope Urban II called for the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont in November 1095.

questions.q: Which King of Scotland and England wrote the 1597 treatise Daemonologie?
questions.explain: James VI of Scotland (later James I of England) published Daemonologie in 1597, reflecting his interest in witchcraft.

questions.q: In which year did the First Crusade capture Jerusalem?
questions.explain: The crusaders stormed and captured Jerusalem on 15 July 1099, establishing Christian rule in the Holy City.

questions.q: Polish independence from communism was spearheaded by which trade union movement?
questions.explain: Solidarity, led by Lech Walesa, drove Poland's break from communist rule by 1989.

questions.q: What was the popular name for the European Recovery Program of 1947-48?
questions.explain: The Marshall Plan provided US economic aid to rebuild Western Europe and resist communism.

questions.q: In which year did Napoleon Bonaparte seize power in the coup of 18-19 Brumaire?
questions.explain: Napoleon overthrew the Directory in the coup of Brumaire (9-10 November 1799), establishing the Consulate with himself as First Consul.

questions.q: In which years did the Berlin Blockade and Airlift take place?
questions.explain: The Berlin Blockade ran from June 1948 to May 1949, countered by the Western airlift.

questions.q: What political entity did the crusaders establish after capturing Constantinople in 1204?
questions.explain: After the 1204 sack, the crusaders founded the Latin Empire of Constantinople, fracturing the Byzantine state.
